summary: Chiyong Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held professorships at the International Buddhist University and Shitennoji Junior College (both attested 1976).

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Kōkōdō under Manshi Kiyozawa. He co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921 and was a professor at Otani University in 1919.

Chizuko Yoshimizu (b. 1959) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Gakushuin University, the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi, and earned a PhD from the University of Vienna, later serving as professor at the University of Tsukuba.

Chlodwig H. Werba (b. 1947) is an Indologist, linguist, and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held a professorial post at the University of Vienna, attested from 1990 to 2006 and in 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung (b. 1981) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Sakya College under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso in 2003.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Kunga Chophel, Geshe Tsechok, Zimwok Rinpoche, and Thubten Gyatso, and served as the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery from 1928.
Chogyū Takayama (1871–1902) was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School and the University of Tokyo.
Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (1829–1870) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under the traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim.
Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon by 2015, where he later became an honorary associate (attested 2019).

Christian Bartholomae (1855–1925) was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A student of Heinrich Hübschmann, he held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, Münster, Giessen, and Heidelberg.

Christian Bernert is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University under Jay L. Garfield and John Powers, later becoming Associate Professor of Philosophy at the College of Charleston.

Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a German scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. Educated at the University of Leipzig, he served as Professor of Eloquence and Poetry at the University of Göttingen and director of its library.

Christian Haskett is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. He studied under Robert A. F. Thurman and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

Christian K. Wedemeyer (b. 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and later served as professor at the University of Chicago.

Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. Educated at Marburg, Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, Munich, Leiden, and Copenhagen, he founded the German Archaeological Institute in 1829.

Christian Lassen (1800–1876) was a Norwegian-born Indologist and linguist who studied at Oslo, Heidelberg, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He succeeded Schlegel as professor of Old Indian language and literature at the University of Bonn in 1840.

Christian Lee Novetzke (b. 1969) works in Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard Divinity School, and Columbia University, later serving as professor at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Washington.
Christian Lindtner (1953–2020) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Copenhagen in 1982 and served there as professor.
